column1: # One row per option `examples/doom/bin/doom.rb` accepts. The audit reads the
# options out of the entry's own tree (StringNodes in `main` that begin with a
# dash) and requires a bijection with this table: an option with no row, or a
# row naming an option the source does not accept, fails the run. That is what
# keeps the table from drifting when the CLI changes.
# `dimension` is what the option varies for the three CORE entries. `reference`
# is a tracked command in this repository that exercises it, or NONE -- and
# NONE is reported, not hidden: it marks a mode this repository cannot
# currently reproduce, which is a fact Stage 2 has to carry rather than

column4: note
The IWAD Full opens and owns; every entry reads from it indirectly through Wad, Level, Textures and Sprites.
Selects the map, which changes every WAD-derived resource's contents and sizes. No tracked command varies it.
Changes thing spawning and monster behaviour inside the tick. No tracked command varies it.
Replaces doom_core_input entirely: the commands come from a demo lump instead of a device. bin/sim_demo.rb replays a recording but is a separate program, not this option.
Adds the angle quantization that doom_core_input must perform when recording, because the recorded game runs on the quantized value.
Supplies synthetic key state, which is how doom_core_input is driven without a human.
Window magnification only. It never reaches a CORE entry; SDL scales the finished frame.

The internal drawing resolution, 320*s by 200*s for s in 1..8. It sizes every render buffer and selects the status-bar shadow path, so it is the one option that changes doom_core_render's allocation. No tracked command varies it.
How many times the loop runs. Full's loop bound, not a CORE input.
Removes the 35 Hz sleep. Only Full reads the clock.
Writes a BMP of a finished frame. Full-side output.
Selects which tics -shot writes. Full-side output.
Per-tic timing TSV. It reads the clock, which happens only in Full.
Per-tic frame hashes. It reads the finished frame buffer after doom_core_render returns.
Selects the Job IR path inside the renderer, which is a different set of reachable definitions for the same entry.

Selects decision 0008's route: before the first tic Full builds the original objects and prepares the session from them, and every tic then runs only through doom_core_input, doom_core_step and doom_core_render in job mode 1. It changes which program runs the tic, not what any entry receives.
Builds the job list without drawing, then draws on the GPU and falls back to the CPU executor per frame. The status bar and HUD stay CPU in both cases, so doom_core_render must cover them either way.
Path to the GPU kernel. Full opens it.
Path to the GPU entry table. Full reads it.
IREE device URI. Full selects it.
